Head of Digital Marketing 
 Total Life · Vancouver· Full-time
 Most marketers pick one side: creative or analytical. We need someone who refuses to choose. 
 Total Life is a national behavioral health telehealth company built for adults in their later years. We offer therapy in all 50 states and DC through 200+ licensed clinicians, and we accept Medicare and most major insurance plans, so care is affordable for the people who need it most. We’re adding psychiatry, longevity, and weight-loss services state by state. Our audience is one of the most underserved, and most overlooked, in digital marketing. Whoever learns to reach them well will build something few people have.
 We are growing quickly. Total Life ranks in the top 10 of the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 (Canada) and #5 in healthcare on the Inc. 5000 . We have also been named to the C100 and are a member of the AARP AgeTech Collaborative. We are now entering our next phase of hypergrowth, and we need a technical leader to build what comes next.
 We’re hiring our Head of Digital Marketing to own paid acquisition end to end: strategy, creative, launch, optimization, and reporting. You’ll work directly with the leadership and have real authority over budget, tools, and direction.
 What you’ll own 
 Paid and organic acquisition across Meta, Google, and TikTok. You’ll plan, build, launch, and scale campaigns, deciding where every dollar goes and defending those calls with data.
 The full funnel, from first impression to booked appointment. Landing pages, intake flows, retargeting, and email and SMS nurture are all yours to test and rebuild. You know the ad is only half the job.
 An AI-powered creative engine. You’ll use AI tools to generate, version, and test ad creative and copy at volume, and you’ll build a system that keeps every asset organized and findable so the library becomes a compounding advantage.
 Reporting the team actually uses. You’ll build clean dashboards and weekly reports that tie spend to cost per booked patient and patient value, not just clicks and impressions.
 A testing culture. You’ll run a steady pipeline of experiments on audiences, hooks, offers, and pages, document what works, and kill what doesn’t quickly.
 Staying ahead of the platforms. Algorithms, ad policies, and tools change monthly. You’ll know before your competitors do and adjust before performance slips.
 You’re the person we’re looking for if 
 You’ve personally run and scaled paid campaigns on Meta, Google, and TikTok, and you can show us results with real numbers.
 You get as excited about a beautiful ad as about a 20% drop in cost per acquisition, and you think the two are connected.
 You live in the data: attribution, cohorts, funnel conversion rates, and the story behind a spreadsheet.
 You already use AI tools daily for creative, copy, analysis, or automation, and you’re always trying new ones.
 You tinker. You’ve built a landing page, rigged a tracking setup, or automated a workflow because you wanted to see whether you could.
 You know what changed on each platform in the last 90 days without having to look it up.
 You can work independently with high ownership and low ego. You’d rather show results than talk about them.
 Bonus points 
 Experience marketing in healthcare, telehealth, or another regulated category, including HIPAA-safe tracking and health ad policies on Meta and Google
 Experience reaching older adults or their adult children
 Comfort with landing-page builders, WordPress, HubSpot or similar CRMs, GHL, and analytics tools such as GA4 and Looker Studio
 Why join us 
 Your work gets older adults to mental health care they’d otherwise go without, and you’ll see the impact in patients booked.
 You’ll have real ownership: your strategy, your stack, your tests.
 Your playbook will shape the company as we expand into new services and states.
 Competitive compensation with salary, performance bonus and equity!

Job Description Summary 
Join the innovative Grid Automation Technology team! We are seeking an experienced embedded DSP Developer to join our dynamic team in creating the building blocks to enable digital transformation in the power grid, focused on signal digitization, protection & control infrastructure devices!
The ideal candidate will possess a deep understanding of embedded systems architecture with DSP, software and hardware architectures, and protection application knowledge within the Transmission & Distribution power-system domain. You will be responsible for executing a robust process of design, creation, and optimization of embedded systems, consisting of identification and quantification of system requirements, creation of alternate system design concepts, performance of design trade studies, selection and implementation of the best designs and verification that the design is properly integrated and executed. This process proceeds from concept to production to operation, based on strategies for the power industry.
As part of a multi-developer firmware team the major responsibilities will include architecture, analysis, design of embedded solutions for Square/UR product line. The Senior Staff Developer – Embedded SW Development will report to the Senior Embedded SW Manager. 
 Job Description 
 Essential Responsibilities: 
 In this role, you will: 
 Analyze complex challenging requirements to architect effective DSP design solutions making up the overall system architecture including hardware, embedded DSP software, software tools, V&V and test rigs.
 Provide forward-looking strategies for platforms and technology development, technical risks elimination and insertion, in order to make the platform reliable and the product competitive.
 Drive platform reuse strategies. Making data-driven decisions using defined trade-off criteria.
 Facilitate, drive discussions and steer cross-functional councils to solve issues, drive decisions, gain consensus, and align on technical risk mitigation strategies.
 Communicate complex messages and negotiate with others to adopt a different point of view. Influence peers to take action and negotiate with external partners and vendors.
 Utilize in-depth understanding of key technology challenges to accomplish own work and provide direction to cross-functional teams.
 Application of technical skills and analytic thinking required to solve problems, using multiple internal sources and some external sources to arrive at decisions.
 Define architecture enablers and collaborate with ART Product Owners and Product Managers on backlog definition and prioritization.
 Provide timely communications on significant issues, risks and/or developments. Maintaining a focus on safety, reliability, performance, and security for embedded systems.
 Capture and elicit detailed requirements from stakeholders to ensure comprehensive understanding and documentation.
 Handle change management and impact analysis. Assessing the effects of modifications on system architecture.
 Act as a resource for colleagues with less experience. Explain difficult information and work to build consensus. Use persuasion skills to influence others on topics within field.
 Basic Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering
 Minimum of 10 years software development experience
 A minimum of 8 years of DSP algorithm design and implementation experience is a must (FFT, IIR, FIR)
 Experience with microprocessors and microcontrollers
 Experience with embedded software development, Assembly, C/C++, VxWorks, Linux, ARM, SHARC, 67xx.
 Experience in code optimization and efficiency improvements 
 Experience using emulators, simulators and software analysis tools
 Knowledge of MATLAB will be an added advantage

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





About the Role



As a Strategic CSM, you'll own the full lifecycle for approximately 100 of our biggest & most important brands. These are the accounts where Owner's platform has the deepest impact. In an intensively competitive market a great CSM relationship is the difference between a customer who stays and grows and one who churns.



This is not a "check the box" CS role. You'll operate as a trusted business consultant for restaurant owners. You'll analyze their performance data, shape their marketing strategy, troubleshoot their operations, and build the kind of relationship where they call you before they call anyone else. You'll also help build the playbooks, processes, and institutional knowledge that make the Strategic motion repeatable as we scale.



We're looking for someone who thrives with a high volume of relationships. Who can handle the pace and ambiguity of a startup, and someone who finds real satisfaction in helping small business owners win.



What You'll Do



Own your book. Manage a named portfolio of ~100 parent restaurant brands. You're their person — the single point of accountability for their success on the Owner platform, from onboarding through renewal and beyond.



Be the consultant they don't have. Most independent restaurant owners don't have a CMO, a CTO, or a data analyst. You'll fill all three gaps — translating platform data into plain-language recommendations on online ordering performance, marketing campaigns, SEO, and guest engagement. You'll lead kickoff calls, performance reviews, and proactive check-ins that are grounded in their numbers and focused on driving results.



Protect and grow revenue. Own retention and growth for your book. Proactively identify churn signals using data points, intervene before problems escalate, and build the case for why Owner is driving real value. When a customer is considering leaving, you'll lead the save conversation with data and empathy.



Run business reviews that matter. Prepare and deliver recurring performance reviews for your key accounts. You’ll lead honest conversations about what's working, what's not, and what to do next. Tie every recommendation back to the restaurant's actual business goals: more orders, more repeat guests, more revenue through their own channels.



Build the motion. The Strategic CSM function is still maturing. You'll have real input into the playbooks, engagement models, and operational systems that define how this team works. If you see a better way to segment, prioritize, or engage, you'll have a seat at the table to propose it and the support to build it.



Partner cross-functionally. Work closely with Sales, Partnerships, Launch, Marketing, SEO, and Product to advocate for your customers and close the loop on their feedback. Escalate intelligently. Bring patterns, not just problems.



What You Bring



3+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related customer-facing role in B2B or B2B2C SaaS. You've managed a book of business, owned retention metrics, and operated with real accountability for outcomes.



Experience managing multi-location or high-value accounts. You know what it means to manage complexity across locations, stakeholders, and priorities — and you don't lose the thread.



A consultative, data-informed approach. You're comfortable pulling a report, identifying the story in the numbers, and translating that into a recommendation a restaurant owner can act on. You don't just present data — you interpret it.



The ability to handle hard conversations with grace. You've navigated cancellation calls, retention negotiations, and de-escalations. You don't shy away from conflict — you lean into it with empathy and clarity.



Strong prioritization instincts. With ~100 accounts, you can't go deep on everything every day. You know how to segment by risk and opportunity, manage your time ruthlessly, and still make every customer feel like they matter.



Comfort with a fast-moving environment. You'll work daily in Salesforce, Notion, Slack, SalesLoft, and Sigma. You’ll have 10-20 calls per day with customers. You’ll find problems you don’t have answers for but are expected to find them. You don’t have to be an expert on day 1 but you’re expected to be the person who hustles each day to get better.



Communication skills that flex. You can write a crisp email to a restaurant owner, lead a compelling business review, and summarize a complex situation for your manager in the same morning.



Nice to Have



 - Experience in the restaurant, food, or hospitality industry

 - Familiarity with online ordering platforms, POS systems, or restaurant marketing tools

 - Experience working in a high-growth startup where processes are still being built

 - Bilingual (English/Spanish) — a meaningful share of our restaurant partners are Spanish-speaking owners



What Success Looks Like



You'll be measured on the outcomes that matter most to our customers and our business:

 - Revenue retention - you keep your book healthy and growing

 - Customer engagement and product adoption - your customers are actually using the platform, and you know why (or why not)

 - Risk reduction - You proactively identify and reduce the overall risk for our strategic portfolio



A Note About This Role


We'll be honest: this is a demanding job. You'll carry a large book, move fast, and wear a lot of hats. Priorities will shift. You'll be expected to operate with high ownership and minimal hand-holding.

But if you're the kind of person who finds energy in helping small business owners grow — who gets a genuine thrill from seeing a restaurant's online orders climb because of a recommendation you made — this is one of the most rewarding roles in customer success. You'll have a meaningful impact on real businesses, real influence on how we build this function, and a front-row seat to one of the most exciting platform plays in the restaurant industry.



Compensation and benefits



The estimated base salary range for this role is $90K-100K USD / $125,500-$137,000 CAD. Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, work from anywhere (100% remote workplace), unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!






Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

ValPay builds embedded payments for software companies. Our PayFac-as-a-Service model lets ISVs offer payments to their merchants under their own brand, while we handle underwriting, compliance, and risk. Our partners serve healthcare, legal, hospitality, professional services, and other vertical markets.
 Launching a payments product is the easy part. The value is created when ISV partners go live, their merchants enroll, and transactions flow. We’re hiring a product marketing Lead whose success is measured by adoption: how quickly and how deeply partners and merchants use our products.
 You’ll own positioning, launches, and lifecycle marketing across our vertical markets and across North America, Europe, and APAC. You’ll report to the CEO and work closely with product, sales, partnerships, the ISV channel team, and operations. 
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
 What we value 
 Sound judgment and attention to detail.
 Measuring success by what customers do, not by what we shipped.
 Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results.
 The honesty to say when something isn’t working, including your own work.
 What you’ll do 
 Drive partner and merchant adoption: You’ll own the adoption journey end to end: signature, integration, go-live, first transaction, merchant enrollment, and expansion. The hardest gap is between “integrated” and “actively transacting,” and you’ll be the person who finds out where partners and merchants stall and designs programs to close it. That means lifecycle campaigns, onboarding content, and activation playbooks for two audiences at once: the ISV partner and the merchants who use their software. With the ISV channel team, you’ll run co-marketing and merchant-enrollment campaigns that lift penetration within each partner’s customer base.
 Measure adoption and act on it: You’ll build and maintain the adoption dashboard: activation rate, time to first transaction, attach and penetration rate, volume per merchant, feature adoption, and cohort retention. You’ll use that data to segment partners and merchants, flag at-risk accounts, and surface expansion opportunities, then take what you find to the teams who can act on it.
 Own positioning and messaging: You’ll develop the positioning, value propositions, and messaging for each product and vertical, and for new verticals and markets as we enter them. A central part of this is explaining clearly how our embedded payments offering differs from horizontal PayFacs, processors, and ISOs. You’ll translate technical capabilities into the outcomes ISVs and merchants care about: revenue share, retention, cleaner reconciliation, and faster onboarding.
 Run launches built around activation: You’ll lead launch plans for new products, features, verticals, and regions. Every launch gets adoption targets and a 30/60/90-day activation plan, not only awareness goals. You’ll also make sure what we’re building is communicated publicly, online and through partners. You’ll adapt messaging to regional regulatory and market conditions, and work with product, finance, risk, and support so that each launch is commercially and operationally ready before it goes out.
 Equip sales, partnerships, and support: You’ll create the sales playbooks, pitch decks, battlecards, case studies, ROI calculators, and objection-handling guides that sales and partnership teams use, and equip support to explain the products as well. You’ll train teams to sell for activation, not just signature. You’ll run win/loss and churn analysis and feed what you learn back into positioning and the product.
 Represent the market inside the company: You’ll track competitors, pricing, interchange, and regulatory developments, and be the voice of the market and of adoption data in product planning. When acquisitions or product consolidations happen, you’ll support portfolio and integration messaging.
 What you’ll bring 
 At least 3 years of experience in product marketing at a B2B software, fintech, or payments company.
 A track record of running launches and measuring them on adoption or usage, not only on awareness.
 Experience marketing to two audiences at once, such as partners and their customers, or platforms and their users.
 Working knowledge of how card payments work, or the ability to learn it quickly and explain it accurately.
 Comfort with data. You can define a metric, build or spec a dashboard, and draw a conclusion from it.
 Strong writing. You can turn a technical capability into a clear business case for a software company or a small-business owner.
 Experience building sales enablement that teams actually used.
 You can take a loosely defined goal, set your own plan, and finish it.
 You use AI tools every day for research, drafting, and analysis, and you check what they produce.
 Useful experience 
 Embedded payments, PayFac, or ISV channel experience.
 Lifecycle or onboarding marketing in a partner-led business.
 Marketing in healthcare, legal, hospitality, or professional services software.
 Launching products in Europe or APAC.
 Running win/loss or churn analysis programs.
 Hands-on experience with SQL, a BI tool, or marketing automation.
 Portfolio or integration messaging after an acquisition.
 Who will enjoy this role 
 You notice when a partner has been live for two months and only a handful of their merchants have enrolled, and you want to know why. Is it the pitch, the onboarding, the partner’s own sales team, or the product?
 In the same week you might rebuild a merchant onboarding email sequence, pull cohort data for the CEO, train a partnership team on a new vertical, and rewrite a battlecard after a lost deal to a horizontal processor.
 The scope is wide for one person, and adoption is a harder target than launch coverage. You’ll be judged on numbers you influence but don’t fully control, which means working through partners, product, and sales to move them. Priorities will shift with the roadmap and with acquisitions.
 Why this role matters 
 ValPay is building products and features for software partners across several verticals and regions. That work has limited impact unless partners and merchants know about it, understand it, and use it.
 You’ll work directly with the CEO to decide how our products are positioned and how each launch turns into transactions. Your work affects how quickly partners go live, how many of their merchants enroll, and how much volume flows through the platform. You’ll have the authority to set the story and change it when the adoption data says so.
 _______________________________________________________________________________________
 ValPay conçoit des solutions de paiement intégrées pour les entreprises de logiciels. Notre modèle PayFac-as-a-Service permet aux éditeurs de logiciels (ISV) d’offrir des paiements à leurs commerçants sous leur propre marque, pendant que nous prenons en charge la souscription, la conformité et la gestion des risques. Nos partenaires servent les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, des services professionnels et d’autres marchés verticaux.
 Lancer un produit de paiement, c’est la partie facile. La valeur se crée lorsque les ISV partenaires sont mis en service, que leurs commerçants adhèrent et que les transactions circulent. Nous recherchons une personne responsable du marketing produit dont le succès se mesure à l’adoption : la rapidité et la profondeur avec lesquelles les partenaires et les commerçants utilisent nos produits.
 Vous serez responsable du positionnement, des lancements et du marketing du cycle de vie dans l’ensemble de nos marchés verticaux, en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes produit, ventes, partenariats, canal ISV et opérations.
 L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat.
 Ce qui compte pour nous 
 Un bon jugement et le souci du détail.
 Mesurer le succès à ce que font les clients, et non à ce que nous avons livré.
 Prendre ses responsabilités et mener le travail à terme sans qu’on ait à faire de relances.
 Comprendre comment l’entreprise génère des revenus et se soucier des résultats.
 L’honnêteté de dire quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas, y compris dans son propre travail.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Stimuler l’adoption par les partenaires et les commerçants : Vous serez responsable de tout le parcours d’adoption : signature, intégration technique, mise en service, première transaction, adhésion des commerçants et expansion. L’écart le plus difficile à combler se situe entre « intégré » et « en transaction active », et c’est vous qui déterminerez où les partenaires et les commerçants stagnent et qui concevrez des programmes pour combler cet écart. Cela comprend des campagnes de cycle de vie, du contenu d’accueil et d’intégration (onboarding) et des guides d’activation pour deux publics à la fois : l’ISV partenaire et les commerçants qui utilisent son logiciel. Avec l’équipe du canal ISV, vous mènerez des campagnes de comarketing et d’adhésion des commerçants qui augmentent le taux de pénétration au sein de la clientèle de chaque partenaire.
 Mesurer l’adoption et agir en conséquence : Vous créerez et tiendrez à jour le tableau de bord de l’adoption : taux d’activation, délai avant la première transaction, taux de rattachement et de pénétration, volume par commerçant, adoption des fonctionnalités et rétention par cohorte. Vous utiliserez ces données pour segmenter les partenaires et les commerçants, repérer les comptes à risque et faire ressortir les occasions d’expansion, puis vous transmettrez vos constats aux équipes qui peuvent agir.
 Définir le positionnement et les messages : Vous élaborerez le positionnement, les propositions de valeur et les messages pour chaque produit et chaque marché vertical, ainsi que pour les nouveaux marchés à mesure que nous y entrons. Un volet central de ce travail consiste à expliquer clairement en quoi notre offre de paiements intégrés se distingue des PayFac horizontaux, des processeurs de paiement et des ISO. Vous traduirez les capacités techniques en résultats qui comptent pour les ISV et les commerçants : partage des revenus, fidélisation, rapprochement simplifié et intégration plus rapide.
 Mener des lancements axés sur l’activation : Vous dirigerez les plans de lancement des nouveaux produits, fonctionnalités, marchés verticaux et régions. Chaque lancement comporte des cibles d’adoption et un plan d’activation sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, et pas seulement des objectifs de notoriété. Vous veillerez aussi à ce que ce que nous construisons soit communiqué publiquement, en ligne et par l’intermédiaire des partenaires. Vous adapterez les messages aux conditions réglementaires et commerciales de chaque région, et travaillerez avec les équipes produit, finances, risques et soutien pour que chaque lancement soit prêt sur les plans commercial et opérationnel avant sa sortie.
 Outiller les équipes des ventes, des partenariats et du soutien : Vous créerez les guides de vente, présentations, fiches concurrentielles, études de cas, calculateurs de RCI et guides de réponse aux objections qu’utilisent les équipes des ventes et des partenariats, et vous outillerez également l’équipe du soutien pour qu’elle puisse expliquer les produits. Vous formerez les équipes à vendre en visant l’activation, et pas seulement la signature. Vous mènerez des analyses des gains et des pertes ainsi que de l’attrition, et réinjecterez vos apprentissages dans le positionnement et le produit.
 Représenter le marché au sein de l’entreprise : Vous suivrez les concurrents, les prix, les frais d’interchange et l’évolution de la réglementation, et serez la voix du marché et des données d’adoption dans la planification des produits. Lors d’acquisitions ou de regroupements de produits, vous soutiendrez les messages liés au portefeuille et à l’intégration.
 Ce que vous apporterez 
 Au moins trois ans d’expérience en marketing produit dans une entreprise de logiciels B2B, de technologie financière ou de paiements.
 Une expérience concrète de lancements dont le succès a été mesuré par l’adoption ou l’utilisation, et pas seulement par la notoriété.
 De l’expérience à faire du marketing auprès de deux publics à la fois, par exemple des partenaires et leurs clients, ou des plateformes et leurs utilisateurs.
 Une connaissance pratique du fonctionnement des paiements par carte, ou la capacité de l’acquérir rapidement et de l’expliquer avec justesse.
 De l’aisance avec les données. Vous savez définir un indicateur, concevoir ou spécifier un tableau de bord et en tirer une conclusion.
 D’excellentes aptitudes en rédaction. Vous savez transformer une capacité technique en argumentaire d’affaires clair pour une entreprise de logiciels ou le propriétaire d’une petite entreprise.
 De l’expérience dans la création d’outils d’habilitation des ventes que les équipes ont réellement utilisés.
 Vous savez prendre un objectif vaguement défini, établir votre propre plan et le mener à terme.
 Vous utilisez des outils d’IA tous les jours pour la recherche, la rédaction et l’analyse, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
 Atouts 
 Expérience en paiements intégrés, avec des PayFac ou dans un canal ISV.
 Marketing du cycle de vie ou de l’accueil et de l’intégration des clients dans une entreprise axée sur les partenaires.
 Marketing de logiciels dans les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration ou des services professionnels.
 Lancement de produits en Europe ou en Asie-Pacifique.
 Mise en place de programmes d’analyse des gains et des pertes ou de l’attrition.
 Expérience pratique de SQL, d’un outil de veille d’affaires (BI) ou d’automatisation du marketing.
 Messages liés au portefeuille ou à l’intégration à la suite d’une acquisition.
 Ce poste vous plaira si… 
 Vous remarquez qu’un partenaire est en service depuis deux mois et que seule une poignée de ses commerçants ont adhéré, et vous voulez comprendre pourquoi. Est-ce l’argumentaire, l’accueil et l’intégration, l’équipe de vente du partenaire ou le produit?
 Au cours d’une même semaine, vous pourriez refaire une séquence de courriels d’accueil pour les commerçants, extraire des données de cohortes pour le chef de la direction, former une équipe de partenariats sur un nouveau marché vertical et réécrire une fiche concurrentielle après avoir perdu un contrat au profit d’un processeur horizontal.
 La portée du poste est vaste pour une seule personne, et l’adoption est une cible plus difficile à atteindre que la visibilité d’un lancement. Vous serez évalué(e) sur des résultats que vous influencez sans les contrôler entièrement, ce qui veut dire que vous devrez passer par les partenaires, l’équipe produit et les ventes pour les faire bouger. Les priorités évolueront au gré de la feuille de route et des acquisitions.
 Pourquoi ce poste est important 
 ValPay développe des produits et des fonctionnalités pour des partenaires logiciels dans plusieurs marchés verticaux et régions. Ce travail a peu d’impact si les partenaires et les commerçants ne le connaissent pas, ne le comprennent pas et ne l’utilisent pas.
 Vous travaillerez directement avec le chef de la direction pour décider du positionnement de nos produits et de la façon dont chaque lancement se traduit en transactions. Votre travail influence la rapidité avec laquelle les partenaires sont mis en service, le nombre de leurs commerçants qui adhèrent et le volume qui circule sur la plateforme. Vous aurez l’autorité nécessaire pour définir le discours et le modifier lorsque les données d’adoption l’indiquent.

 Title: Manager, People & Culture 
 Employer: Tracxtion 
 Team: People & Culture 
 Hybrid: 3 days in-office weekly 
 Company Overview 
 Tracxtion is a next-generation hybrid agency network built for the evolving landscape of customer experience and brand engagement. We help brands navigate a world where traditional media and marketing boundaries have blurred. 
 By bringing together strategy, creativity, media, digital capabilities, and AI-enabled execution, Tracxtion delivers measurable results through a hybrid approach that combines exceptional human talent with cutting-edge tools and partnerships. From AI-powered advertising and content creation to media planning, experiential marketing, and in-store retail solutions, we partner with leading brands to create innovative, scalable, and impactful omnichannel experiences. 
 Role Overview 
 The Manager, People & Culture plays a critical role in delivering high-quality HR support and people programming across an assigned portfolio of 3 Traction Entities. 
 Reporting to the Senior Director, People & Culture, this role combines strategic business partnership with hands-on execution. The Manager will support leaders, managers, and employees throughout the full employee lifecycle while contributing to broader People & Culture initiatives across the organization. 
 This role carries entity-specific accountability and requires the Manager to develop a strong understanding of each assigned agency's business, culture, workforce, and people priorities. 
 A key component of this role is HRIS ownership. The Manager will be accountable for data integrity, workflow configuration, process standardization, and system adoption within HiBob across their assigned entities. They will ensure the HRIS is not simply maintained but actively leveraged to improve people operations, reporting, and the overall employee experience. 
 Core Responsibilities 
 Business Partnership and Manager Enablement 
 Act as the day-to-day People & Culture partner for department leaders and people managers across assigned Canadian entities. 
 Build trusted relationships with leaders and develop a strong understanding of their business priorities, workforce needs, and team dynamics. 
 Coach managers through performance conversations, employee development, team challenges, and people leadership decisions. 
 Advise leaders on organizational matters, including role design, workforce planning, headcount needs, reporting structures, and team changes. 
 Use people data, employee feedback, and business insights to identify trends and proactively recommend practical solutions. 
 Support leaders in applying policies, programs, and employment practices consistently and fairly. 
 Employee Relations and Compliance 
 Manage employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including performance management, workplace concerns, investigations, accommodations, leaves, and terminations. 
 Ensure consistent, compliant application of policies and employment practices across applicable Canadian jurisdictions. 
 Maintain current knowledge of Canadian employment legislation and evolving workplace requirements. 
 Escalate complex or high-risk matters to the Senior Director, People & Culture with well-documented context, risk considerations, and recommended approaches. 
 Prepare and maintain accurate, confidential, and audit-ready employee relations documentation. 
 Partner with legal counsel or other external advisors when directed. 
 HRIS Ownership, Workflows and Data Integrity 
 Serve as the HiBob lead for assigned entities, with accountability for data integrity, organizational structure accuracy, and employee record completeness across the employee lifecycle. 
 Build, configure, test, and maintain HiBob workflows, including onboarding and offboarding processes, approval chains, document generation, employee changes, leaves, and exits. 
 Design and manage HiBob cycles for performance reviews, goal setting, compensation reviews, employee check-ins, and other people programs. 
 Ensure all cycles are appropriately scoped, sequenced, tested, and communicated to stakeholders. 
 Conduct regular HRIS audits to identify and resolve data discrepancies, outdated records, organizational misalignments, and missing documentation. 
 Partner with the People & Culture Coordinator to establish and maintain clear data-entry standards and standard operating procedures. 
 Act as an internal subject matter expert on HiBob functionality, troubleshooting system issues and escalating platform-level concerns when required. 
 Identify opportunities to automate manual People & Culture processes, improve workflows, and reduce administrative burden. 
 Maintain consistent data structures that support accurate reporting on headcount, turnover, workforce changes, and other key people metrics. 
 Champion HRIS adoption and ensure employee changes, approvals, and documentation are processed through established systems rather than off-system workarounds. 
 People Program Delivery 
 Lead the delivery of core People & Culture programs across assigned entities, including performance cycles, engagement surveys, onboarding, offboarding, and recognition initiatives. 
 Partner with the Senior Director, People & Culture on enterprise-wide initiatives, including compensation cycles, policy updates, organizational programs, and learning and development. 
 Support the administration and employee communication of Canadian benefits, perks, and leave programs. 
 Analyze program feedback and participation data to identify opportunities for improvement. 
 Develop and maintain People & Culture workflows, manager toolkits, templates, standard operating procedures, and employee resources. 
 Ensure programs are delivered consistently while allowing for appropriate entity-specific practices and needs. 
 Culture, Engagement and Inclusion 
 Champion inclusive employment practices and help embed each entity’s culture and values throughout the employee experience. 
 Support leaders with employee engagement action planning and track progress against agreed priorities. 
 Partner on diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging initiatives, events, and employment practices. 
 Identify opportunities to strengthen employee connection, communication, recognition, and engagement across assigned entities. 
 Help leaders navigate change in a clear, thoughtful, and employee-focused manner. 
 Team and Operational Contribution 
 Provide guidance and coaching to People & Culture Coordinators, Specialists, and other junior team members supporting the same entity portfolio. 
 Participate in cross-functional People & Culture projects and enterprise initiatives as a key contributor. 
 Promote process discipline, documentation, and accountability across the People & Culture function. 
 Help establish scalable and consistent practices across a growing, multi-entity organization. 
 Balance strategic priorities with the hands-on operational requirements of a fast-moving agency environment. 
 Qualifications and Experience 
 3+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least one year in an HR Manager, HR Business Partner, or equivalent role. 
 Demonstrated experience supporting Canadian employees and leaders across the full employee lifecycle. 
 Strong knowledge of Canadian employment legislation and HR practices across multiple provinces. 
 Proven experience managing employee relations matters, workplace investigations, accommodations, performance management, and employment terminations. 
 Strong track record of coaching managers and providing practical, business-minded HR advice. 
 Experience working in an agency, media, creative, marketing, or fast-paced professional services environment is preferred. 
 Demonstrated HRIS expertise, with HiBob experience strongly preferred. 
 Experience configuring workflows, building program cycles, conducting data audits, and maintaining HRIS standards in a multi-entity environment. 
 Strong systems orientation and the ability to identify data gaps, improve processes, and encourage consistent system adoption. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to handle sensitive matters with sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism. 
 Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple stakeholders and entities. 
 CHRP designation, or progress toward completion, is considered an asset. 
 Proficiency with HiBob, ADP, and Microsoft 365. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Leaders view the Manager as a trusted, practical, and responsive People & Culture partner. 
 Employee relations matters are managed consistently, thoughtfully, and in compliance with Canadian employment requirements. 
 HiBob data is accurate, complete, and reliable across assigned entities. 
 People processes are increasingly standardized, automated, and managed through established systems. 
 Programs are delivered effectively and adapted appropriately to the needs of each entity. 
 Managers have the tools, guidance, and confidence needed to lead their teams successfully. 
 SALT XC, Tracxtion are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity and to attracting and retaining the most qualified employees regardless of race, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, age or disability.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Role Overview:

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Safety for Agents team, you will make a meaningful impact on the development of better, fairer, more trustworthy, and more secure Large Language Models (LLMs). Your primary focus will be on data generation, post-training algorithms, and evaluation methods to ensure Safety in the next generation of models that can access external resources and take actions in the world. You will work closely with other cross-functional machine learning teams and data annotation teams, and will also collaborate with product and policy teams.

This role combines expertise in machine learning, ethical and responsible AI, experimental design, and data generation and management.

It will require curiosity to tackle totally new scientific problems, engineering skills to implement the pieces we need to test solutions to these, and a desire to dive into messy data and results. You will be on a small team with a lot of autonomy and decision-making power, responsible for making the next generation of LLMs better for society as a whole.



Please Note: The existing team work in offices in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Toronto, and New York, but we also embrace being remote-friendly! For this role you need to have ~50% working day overlap with UK/EU timezone (e.g. US East is fine) but there are otherwise no restrictions on where you can be located for this role.

Key responsibilities:

 - Strong statistical skills and experience evaluating scientific experiments related to data collection and model performance.

 - Extremely strong software engineering skills.

 - Strong expertise in designing and conducting data collection tasks, including working with human annotators.

 - Experience analyzing datasets with respect to their quality, biases, and suitability for training ML models.

 - Hands-on experience training large language models (LLMs) on distributed training infrastructures.

 - Familiarity with evaluating and improving the generalizability and robustness of ML systems.

 - Proficiency in programming languages such as Python and ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX).

 - Excellent communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and present findings.

 - One or more papers at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).

This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 What You'll Do:
 Act as the technical expert for the Network 2.0 ZTNA program — own the architecture, lead build reviews, establish engineering standards, and address any critical issues during implementation.
 Build and validate the full ZTNA architecture across all primary and international sites — defining network zones, segmentation policy, and device posture requirements that eliminate lateral movement risk.
 Manage Palo Alto Panorama at the platform level — template hierarchy, device group creation, policy distribution oversight, and configuration drift prevention across all on-premises and cloud-connected NGFWs.
 Develop the AWS and Palo Alto Panorama cloud integration — detailing how cloud-native firewall policy, VPC topology, and on-premises ZTNA fabric combine within a unified enforcement plane.
 Lead the Palo Alto Cloud Identity Engine (CIE) architecture (Year 2, joint with IAM): construct the identity-to-network enforcement model, compose the network zone taxonomy, and direct the IP-to-identity rule migration that phases out all IP-based user firewall rules.
 Direct GlobalProtect architecture decisions — agent configuration, split tunneling policy, certificate trust chain, and version compliance standards upheld through Intune.
 Develop and keep current the network architecture documents, decision records, and runbook library that the broader team relies on to carry out tasks. You establish the standard; the team adheres to it.
 Lead the global site topology mapping effort by detailing all international sites. Define the tiered support model and produce the hardware refresh sequencing plan linked to the ZTNA rollout waves.
 Partner with the Automation / Network Reliability Engineer to build self-healing policy frameworks, Panorama API automation patterns, and CI/CD pipeline standards for network configuration changes.

 10+ years of enterprise network engineering with demonstrated depth in large-scale architecture building — not just operations.
 Advanced knowledge of Palo Alto NGFW and Panorama — template hierarchy, device groups, security policy development, NAT, decryption policy, and multi-vsys environments.
 Proven ZTNA architecture experience — you have built a ZTNA deployment, not just configured one; you understand the segmentation model, the policy logic, and the failure modes.
 Comprehensive knowledge of GlobalProtect — covering agent architecture, gateway configuration, certificate trust, split tunneling policy, and troubleshooting issues across diverse endpoint types on a large scale.
 AWS network architecture hands-on — VPC build, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, AWS Network Firewall, and cloud-native connectivity patterns that integrate with on-premises enforcement.
 Understanding of identity-to-network enforcement patterns — how identity signals (Okta groups, Entra device compliance, CIE) translate into firewall policy and how that architecture scales.
 Grasp of SD-WAN concepts and Prisma SD-WAN or equivalent — intelligent path selection, application-aware routing, and WAN optimization in a multi-site enterprise.

SENIOR STRATEGIC IMPLEMENTATION SPECIALIST, AMERICAS 

Hi! I’m Morgan, the Manager of Strategic Implementations here at Ashby. Our customers are at the center of everything we do, and that’s especially true during implementation. We take pride in being responsive, collaborative partners who focus not just on delivery, but on doing things thoughtfully. This role plays a critical part in ensuring our new customers start off with a strong foundation and a clear path forward. I’m thrilled to be hiring our next Implementation Specialist. As part of our growing Professional Services team within Ashby’s Customer Success organization, you’ll play a key role early in the customer journey - ultimately helping to elevate the entire customer experience.

The Ashby team has grown rapidly over the last few years, and we're not slowing down: we added more than 2,100 new customers in the last year alone and now support over 5,000 customers, with ARR growing much faster than 100% year over year. We're expecting similarly fast growth this year, and every one of those new customers needs a thoughtful implementation to actually get value out of Ashby. We'll share more details once we meet, but you probably have a good idea as to why we're expanding this team!




THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Senior Strategic Implementation Specialist who excels at leading technically complex, hands on implementation projects for B2B SaaS customers. You'll own each implementation from the moment Sales hands it off through go-live; part project manager, part technical expert, and part trusted advisor to the customer!

Six months in, success looks like carrying a full book of 8-12 active implementations, running each customer relationship on your own (kickoff, timeline, follow-through), independently solving complex configuration and workflow challenges, and handling the normal bumps (a slow-to-respond customer, a technical snag, an escalation) without the rest of your book slipping. It also means you're starting to make things better beyond your own accounts: you've found at least one process or documentation gap and fixed it, and you're feeding real customer feedback back to our Product team.




YOU WILL ACHIEVE THIS BY:

 - Managing 8-12 active enterprise implementations at a time (12-16 weeks implementation timeline on average), building each customer's project plan from handoff through go-live, and staying on top of timelines, hurdles, and follow-up along the way

 - Getting genuinely comfortable with the in’s and out’s of how our products work, so you can troubleshoot and advise instead of just walking through a checklist

 - Advising on what’s worked well for similar customers in the past, challenging assumptions when appropriate, and recommending configurations and workflows that balance customer needs with implementation best practices

 - Partnering closely with cross-functional partners across the business, especially Sales and CS to ensure a seamless customer journey, and Product/Engineering to flag real issues and align on a path forward

As you're probably gathering, we're looking for someone who gets energy from both sides of this: the structure of running a tight project plan, and the judgment to rethink that plan when a customer's business genuinely calls for it.

 

If you have the majority of the following, you could be a great fit for this role: 

 - 7+ years of experience in a customer-facing role, with the majority of your focus on leading full-cycle B2B SaaS implementations

 - Proven track record successfully managing upmarket concurrent implementation projects without compromising quality, customer experience, or timelines

 - Experience operating with real autonomy and to own the implementation project plans end-to-end

 - Comfortable getting into the weeds of complex, multi-module software, and building genuine fluency in how it all fits together

 - Resourceful when there's no documented answer; you do your own testing and discovery, then use what you learn to advise customers on best practices and recommendations

 - Data-driven and detail-oriented, with a genuine instinct for coaching customers through unfamiliar territory

If you need someone else to do any of the following, then this role is probably not for you:

 - Independently investigate complex customer questions and become the technical/product subject matter expert during implementations

 - Carry more than a handful of accounts at once (this is a high volume role on a team that moves with urgency)

 - Own the execution of a project plan, not just its design

 - Iterate and improve on existing processes





INSTRUCTIONS

Please take your time with your application and the application questions. Although we use AI to assist in our review, we never use AI to auto-qualify or disqualify candidates. We lay eyes on each and every application, and speak to a very select number of candidates based on the application as a whole. This is an evergreen opening, so there is no need to rush, and there are no prizes for being first!

 


OUR PHILOSOPHY

Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell.

 - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly.

 - We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Operating Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles to get a sense of what we are looking for in folks on the team.

 


THE INTERVIEW

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

 - 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

 - 45 min - Interview with Manager of High Touch Implementations

 - 60 min- Mock Call with an Implementation Specialist and Customer Success Manager

 - Final Round:
   
   - 30 min - Cross-Functional Interview with Head of Professional Services
   
   - 30 min - Product Complexity Interview with VP of Customer Success
   
   - 30 min - Customer Adoption & Enablement with Manager of High Touch Customer Success and a High Touch Customer Success Manager
   
   - 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager

 


BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - You get to sell a product that our prospects & customers are truly excited about.

 - Competitive compensation is offered.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval

About Flinks 
 Flinks is the embedded finance platform that brings together connectivity, intelligence, and payments — giving businesses the infrastructure they need to build and deliver seamless financial experiences at scale.
 As a leader in Open Finance in Canada, we’ve grown since 2016 into one of North America’s most trusted platforms for financial data access, enrichment, and money movement. We work with innovators across many industries, including lending, fintech, banking, insurance, and wealth management.
 Today, our platform connects to 15,000+ financial institutions across North America and powers over 1M monthly connections. We also give our customers unprecedented visibility into 4,500+ real-time financial insights to support smarter decisioning. Companies rely on Flinks to streamline onboarding, verify income, assess credit risk, and power faster payment experiences.
 We’re on a mission to drive financial innovation and help businesses build financial experiences that feel effortless, connected, and customer-first. That’s where you come in.
 The Role
 We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks . You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.
 If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.
 What You'll Do
 Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
 Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
 Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
 Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them .
 Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
 Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).
 What You'll Work On
 You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.
 Key areas of focus include:
 Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data. 
 Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams. 
 Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products. 
 Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads. 
 Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery. 
 Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.
 Our stack
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery and dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana and GCP Logging 
 You don't need experience with every tool listed above - strong Data Engineering fundamentals and experience building production data platforms matter more than direct experience with our exact stack. SQL is the exception : it's a non-negotiable (see Key Requirements). 
 Why This Role
 Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products. 
 High leverage impact — your work enables Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Risk teams to move faster with reliable, trusted data. 
 Real-world scale and complexity — work with large volumes of financial data powering products used by banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across North America. 
 Modern cloud-native environment — build on a modern GCP stack using contemporary data, platform, and machine learning tooling.
 Key Requirements
 Experience: 5+ years of hands-on Data Engineering experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms, pipelines, and warehouse solutions in a cloud environment.
 Data Engineering Expertise: Strong experience with ETL/ELT development, data modeling, schema design, orchestration, data quality, lineage, and warehouse optimization. Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or equivalent modern data tooling is highly desirable.
 Technical Foundation: Expert SQL and strong Python skills, with the ability to build scalable, maintainable, and well-tested data solutions that support both operational and analytical workloads.
 Cloud Data Platforms: Experience working with modern cloud-native data ecosystems, including data warehouses, event-driven architectures, distributed processing, and platform observability.
 Operational Excellence: Demonstrated ownership of production systems, including monitoring, reliability, performance tuning, cost optimization, incident response, and ongoing platform improvements.
 Machine Learning Platform Exposure: Experience supporting machine learning workflows, feature pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or MLOps environments is an asset, but a strong Data Engineering foundation is the primary requirement.
 Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Data Science, Product, Engineering, and QA teams to deliver trusted, scalable, and well-governed data solutions.
 Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in Canada.
 Benefits 
 As part of the total rewards package, Flinks offers:
 Health & Dental coverage as of Day 1
 Flexible Paid Time Off (FTO)
 Remote work environment with frequent in-person gatherings and activities.
 Career development, learning opportunities and growth
 And more

 Chef de file de la finance ouverte (Open Finance) au Canada, nous avons connu une croissance soutenue depuis 2016 pour devenir l’une des plateformes les plus fiables en Amérique du Nord en matière d’accès aux données financières, d’enrichissement des données et de mouvement de fonds. Nous collaborons avec des entreprises innovantes dans de nombreux secteurs, notamment le crédit, les technologies financières (fintech), les services bancaires, l’assurance et la gestion de patrimoine.
 Aujourd’hui, notre plateforme est connectée à plus de 15 000 institutions financières à travers l’Amérique du Nord et soutient plus d’un million de connexions mensuelles. Nous offrons également à nos clients un accès à plus de 4 500 indicateurs financiers en temps réel afin de favoriser une prise de décision plus éclairée. Les entreprises s’appuient sur Flinks pour simplifier l’intégration de leurs utilisateurs, vérifier les revenus, évaluer le risque de crédit et offrir des expériences de paiement plus rapides.
 Notre mission est d’accélérer l’innovation financière et d’aider les entreprises à créer des expériences financières simples, connectées et centrées sur leurs clients. C’est là que vous entrez en jeu.
 Le poste
 Nous recrutons notre Ingénieur(e) principal(e) en données (Plateforme Données / IA) afin d’établir l’ingénierie des données comme une discipline à part entière chez Flinks. Vous serez responsable de la plateforme de données et d’apprentissage automatique qui transforme les modèles en services de production fiables, renforcerez les modèles de données sur lesquels l’entreprise s’appuie et assurerez la connexion entre nos scientifiques des données et les équipes produit.
 Il s’agit d’un rôle à forte autonomie, orienté vers la création de nouvelles fondations : une grande partie de cette infrastructure sera à concevoir, bâtir et faire évoluer par vous, plutôt qu’à hériter d’un environnement existant.
 Si vous aimez être la personne qui rend les données et l’IA prêtes pour la production — pipelines, mise en service des modèles, gouvernance, fiabilité — et que vous souhaitez avoir un impact important sur l’ensemble des capacités de données d’une entreprise, ce rôle est fait pour vous.
 Ce que vous ferez
 Assurer la propriété et l’évolution de la plateforme de données — l’entrepôt BigQuery, les couches de transformation dbt, l’orchestration Airflow / Cloud Composer et les mécanismes d’ingestion Pub/Sub qui alimentent chaque modèle et indicateur. 
 Concevoir, exploiter et faire évoluer la plateforme d’apprentissage automatique — pipelines d’entraînement (Kubeflow sur Vertex AI), mise en service des modèles (FastAPI derrière les points de terminaison Vertex), CI/CD, conteneurisation et contrats typés. Assumer la responsabilité opérationnelle de l’infrastructure de mise en production des modèles afin que leur fiabilité ne repose pas uniquement sur les scientifiques des données. 
 Renforcer et standardiser les modèles de données essentiels aux opérations de l’entreprise — amélioration des schémas, correction des problèmes de qualité des données et mise en place de sources de vérité fiables. 
 Mettre en place des pratiques de gouvernance et d’observabilité des données — intégrer sous une gouvernance appropriée les données qui se trouvent à l’extérieur de l’entrepôt et créer des métriques opérationnelles pour les produits qui n’en disposent pas encore. 
 Standardiser les pratiques d’ingénierie des données à travers les différentes lignes de produits — modèles, outils et pipelines pouvant être réutilisés par les autres équipes. 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de science des données, de développement backend et de produit afin de définir et maintenir le contrat entre producteurs et consommateurs de données (modèles produits par la science des données, consommés ou agrégés en aval et exposés aux clients).
 Ce sur quoi vous travaillerez
 Vous contribuerez à bâtir et à faire évoluer la plateforme de données qui alimente les produits d’intelligence financière de Flinks, soutenant notamment l’enrichissement et la catégorisation des transactions, ainsi que les solutions de gestion du risque et de prise de décision liées aux paiements.
 Les principaux domaines d’intervention incluent :
 Concevoir des pipelines de données évolutifs capables de traiter et de transformer de grands volumes de données financières. 
 Concevoir et maintenir des ensembles de données, modèles de données et pipelines de caractéristiques fiables utilisés par les équipes d’apprentissage automatique et de produit. 
 Améliorer la qualité des données, l’observabilité et les indicateurs opérationnels à travers notre plateforme et nos produits destinés aux clients. 
 Développer des services et infrastructures de données performants et optimisés en coûts afin de soutenir des charges de travail en temps réel et par lots. 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit et Ingénierie afin de permettre le développement de nouvelles capacités et d’accélérer la livraison de produits. 
 Contribuer à l’évolution de l’architecture de notre plateforme de données alors que nous continuons à faire croître nos produits, notre clientèle et nos capacités d’apprentissage automatique.
 Notre environnement technologique
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery et dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub et Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow et FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform et Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana et GCP Logging 
 Vous n’avez pas besoin d’avoir travaillé avec chacun des outils mentionnés ci-dessus. De solides fondations en ingénierie des données et une expérience démontrée dans la conception de plateformes de données en production sont plus importantes qu’une connaissance approfondie de notre pile technologique actuelle. Le SQL constitue toutefois l’exception : il s’agit d’une exigence incontournable (voir les exigences clés). 
 Pourquoi ce poste?
 Responsabilité sur un environnement en construction — contribuez à bâtir et à faire évoluer la plateforme de données qui alimentera la prochaine génération de produits de données et d’intelligence artificielle de Flinks. 
 Impact à fort levier — votre travail permettra aux équipes Science des données, Produit, Ingénierie et Risque d’avancer plus rapidement grâce à des données fiables et dignes de confiance. 
 Échelle et complexité réelles — travaillez avec d’importants volumes de données financières alimentant des produits utilisés par des banques, fintechs et institutions financières partout en Amérique du Nord. 
 Environnement infonuagique moderne — développez des solutions sur une pile technologique GCP moderne utilisant des outils contemporains de données, de plateformes et d’apprentissage automatique.
 Exigences essentielles
 Expérience : 
 Plus de 5 ans d’expérience pratique en ingénierie des données, incluant la conception, le développement et l’exploitation de plateformes de données, de pipelines et de solutions d’entreposage de données en environnement infonuagique.
 Expertise en ingénierie des données : 
 Expérience approfondie en développement ETL/ELT, modélisation de données, conception de schémas, orchestration, qualité des données, traçabilité des données (data lineage) et optimisation d’entrepôts de données. Une expérience avec BigQuery, dbt, Airflow ou des outils modernes équivalents est fortement souhaitée.
 Fondations techniques : 
 Excellente maîtrise du SQL et solides compétences en Python, avec la capacité de concevoir des solutions de données évolutives, maintenables et rigoureusement testées, soutenant à la fois les besoins opérationnels et analytiques.
 Plateformes de données infonuagiques : 
 Expérience avec des écosystèmes de données modernes natifs du nuage, incluant les entrepôts de données, les architectures événementielles, le traitement distribué et les pratiques d’observabilité des plateformes.
 Excellence opérationnelle : 
 Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de systèmes en production, notamment en matière de surveillance, de fiabilité, d’optimisation des performances, de contrôle des coûts, de gestion des incidents et d’amélioration continue des plateformes.
 Expérience liée aux plateformes d’apprentissage automatique : 
 Une expérience soutenant des flux de travail d’apprentissage automatique, des pipelines de caractéristiques, des infrastructures de mise en production de modèles ou des environnements MLOps constitue un atout. Toutefois, une solide expertise en ingénierie des données demeure la principale exigence.
 Collaboration : 
 Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit, Ingénierie et Assurance qualité (QA) afin de livrer des solutions de données fiables, évolutives et bien gouvernées.
 Formation : 
 Baccalauréat en informatique, en ingénierie des données, en génie logiciel ou dans un domaine technique connexe, ou expérience pratique équivalente.
 Autorisation de travail : 
 Doit être légalement autorisé(e) à travailler au Canada.
 Ce que Flinks offre
 Dans le cadre de son programme global de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux, Flinks offre notamment :
 Couverture santé et dentaire dès le premier jour
 Politique de congés flexibles (FTO)
 Environnement de travail à distance avec des rencontres et activités en personne régulières
 Opportunités de développement professionnel, d’apprentissage et de croissance
 Et bien plus encore
 Accessibilité
 Flinks s’engage à offrir des mesures d’adaptation aux personnes en situation de handicap. Si vous avez besoin d’un accommodement dans le cadre du processus de recrutement ou d’emploi, nous travaillerons avec vous afin de répondre à vos besoins.
 Intelligence artificielle et recrutement
 Flinks utilise l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans le cadre de son processus de recrutement afin d’aider à la présélection, à l’évaluation ou à la sélection des candidats.

À propos de Mila 
 Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions au domaine de l’apprentissage profond, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
 Mila s’est donné pour mission d’être un pôle mondial d’avancées scientifiques qui inspire l’innovation et l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) au bénéfice de tous.
 Pour en connaitre davantage, veuillez consulter https://mila.quebec/ 
 Sommaire du poste
 Le Laboratoire d'IA souveraine est une nouvelle initiative de Mila visant à assembler une pile (stack) d'inférence en IA open source, prête pour l'entreprise, que les organisations peuvent déployer et exploiter sur des infrastructures qu'elles contrôlent. Elle regroupe des fonctionnalités telles que la mise en service de modèles (model serving), la recherche d'information (retrieval), l'orchestration d'agents, l'observabilité et un plan de contrôle (control plane) pour opérer ces composants comme un produit cohérent.
 En tant que gestionnaire senior de la livraison technique, vous dirigerez la livraison de bout en bout des déploiements partenaires, depuis la découverte initiale et l'étude de faisabilité jusqu'à la planification, le déploiement, le transfert opérationnel et la revue d'adoption initiale. Vous gérerez plusieurs pilotes et déploiements en production simultanés, en servant de point de contact et de responsabilité principal auprès du partenaire durant la phase active de livraison. Relevant du directeur principal du produit, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'ingénierie et les partenariats pour définir des engagements crédibles, coordonner l'exécution et maintenir l'alignement entre les parties prenantes techniques et exécutives.
 Il s'agit d'un rôle de coordination à forte maîtrise technique. Vous définirez la portée de livraison, les jalons, les responsabilités, les risques et les critères d'acceptation; vous coordonnerez les développeurs et spécialistes réalisant le travail; et vous recommanderez des ajustements lorsque la portée, l'échéancier ou le niveau de préparation ne seront plus réalistes.
 Le succès signifie que les partenaires réalisent des déploiements opérationnels validés selon les critères d'acceptation convenus, commencent à adopter la pile pour leurs cas d'usage visés et sont prêts à l'exploiter. Cela signifie également que chaque déploiement génère des enseignements produits exploitables et améliore les guides pratiques (playbooks), les critères d'acceptation et les pratiques de livraison utilisés avec les futurs partenaires.
 Principales responsabilités
 Mener la phase de découverte initiale auprès des partenaires afin de comprendre le cas d'usage visé, l'environnement de déploiement, les contraintes organisationnelles et les critères de succès, en collaboration avec l'ingénierie pour évaluer la faisabilité avant la prise d'engagements.
 Définir et maintenir les plans de livraison à travers plusieurs déploiements partenaires simultanés, incluant la portée, les jalons, les responsabilités, les dépendances, les besoins en ressources, les risques et les critères d'acceptation.
 Agir en tant que responsable principal vis-à-vis du partenaire durant la livraison active, en communiquant l'avancement, les décisions, les risques et les changements aux équipes techniques et aux sponsors exécutifs.
 Servir de pont principal entre notre équipe interne et l'équipe du partenaire de déploiement tout au long du processus de mise en œuvre.
 Identifier rapidement les risques de livraison et les décisions non tranchées, évaluer leurs implications et recommander des ajustements de portée, de séquence, d'échéancier ou de préparation lorsque les engagements ne sont plus crédibles.
 Mener des sessions de rétroaction structurées avec les administrateurs et utilisateurs des partenaires, en traduisant les constats du déploiement et les retours en problématiques produit et en recommandations.
 Repérer les tendances à travers les déploiements et élaborer des guides pratiques (playbooks), modèles, critères d'acceptation et pratiques de revue réutilisables afin d'améliorer les livraisons futures.

 The Sovereign AI Lab is a new Mila initiative to assemble an enterprise-ready, open-source AI inference stack that organizations can deploy and operate on infrastructure they control.
